newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: U.S. urged to do more in Malaysian wheat market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urged to do more in Malaysian wheat market.

text.p: The U.S. wheat industry needs to do more to dent the strong control of Australian exporters in the Malaysian wheat market, an industry official said on Tuesday.

Neoh Soon Bin, managing director of the Soon Soon Group of Companies in Malaysia, told a conference staged by the U.S. wheat industry that Australia supplies 70 percent of the estimated one million tonnes bought by Malaysia every year.
The U.S. share stands at about 6.4 percent.
Neoh said the U.S. should "grow more hard white wheat in the Pacific Northwest area" since most of Malaysia's wheat goes into the production of noodles.
The U.S. should also transport more of its wheat on Panamax type ships with a capacity of 55,000 tonnes instead of the current Handy sized vessels capable of hauling 25,000 tonnes, he said.

"The Panamax freight favours the United States and Canada," Neoh said, adding that the average freight on a Panamax from the U.S. would reach about US$13-$14 a tonne, almost the same level as that from Australia.
Shipment time from the United States averages 23-24 days compared to around 30 days from wheat from Australia.
